finding.claim: The purge handler calls checkPerm(u, "admin") but discards the boolean result, so the admin check is never enforced. Any user who can reach the endpoint can run purgeAll(). Compare rotateKeys, which correctly returns early when mustPerm fails.
finding.source: Any authenticated (non-admin) user sending a request to the purge endpoint

trace.note: u := userFrom(r) obtains the requesting user from the request context
checkPerm(u, "admin") returns a bool that is ignored; no early return or error response

finding.guards_checked: checkPerm result is unused. mustPerm is not used in purge. No other middleware or auth check is visible in the repo, which contains only handlers.go. Upstream routing or middleware could not be inspected, so a route-level admin guard, if one exists, would mitigate this. By contrast, rotateKeys at line 33 enforces the check properly.

verdict.guard_found: none in repo; checkPerm (handlers.go:12) returns bool but result is discarded at line 26. Route-level middleware not inspectable (only handlers.go exists).
verdict.reason: handlers.go:26 calls checkPerm as a bare statement (it returns a bool at handlers.go:12 and doesn't abort), so purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 runs for any user, unlike rotateKeys, which returns early on mustPerm failure at handlers.go:33-35.

verdict_facts.guard_found: none (checkPerm at handlers.go:26 returns a bool that is discarded; no route-level guard is visible, and the project facts say every handler is reachable unless the code restricts it)
